instruction: Run a speed test at speedtest.net, and record the Ping, Download, and Upload metrics in ~/speed_test_results.txt, with each on its own line and formatted as 'MetricName Value'.

metadata.explanation: This variation uses 'assess' and 'performance' terminology, saves to the home directory directly (~/speed_test_results.txt) instead of a subdirectory, and uses the phrasing 'copy the test results' similar to the original. The task maintains identical complexity - measuring the same three core metrics (Ping, Download, Upload) from speedtest.net. Uses custom check_speedtest_format__26660ad1 metric to verify all three metrics are present with numeric values in the correct format (each metric on its own line with name and value).
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Binary: 1.0 if all three metrics (Ping, Download, Upload) are present in the file with numeric values in the correct format (metric name followed by space/colon and a number), 0.0 otherwise

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts file content from ~/speed_test_results.txt using env.controller.get_file()
Metric correctly validates all three required metrics (Ping, Download, Upload) are present with numeric values
Regex pattern correctly matches format: metric name + optional colon + whitespace + numeric value
Case-insensitive matching provides flexibility for different formatting styles
Handles edge cases correctly (empty file, missing file returns 0.0)
Parameter handling is correct: metric receives rules dict directly from get_rule() as expected_state
Complete coverage: all instruction requirements are verified (file location, 3 metrics, format, numeric values)
Data flow is semantically correct: file read → text parsing → format validation
